name: fpds-level-gauge
title: Level gauge (molecule)
description: A tank's level, its monitor's battery and its days to empty — each in its own cell. — spec: docs/fpds/03-molecules.md:770. Needs fpds-theme.

files.content: import * as React from "react"; import { cn } from "@/lib/utils"; import { PILL_SHAPE, pillColorClass, type PillColor, type PillKind, } from "@/components/ui/pill"; /** * Visual channel a status is rendered in. Deliberately NOT a list of domain * statuses: per the DS's colour governance a status carries no colour until a * usage rule binds it, so the DS ships the channels and each application * declares its own mapping (see `statusTone` in `tables-layout/data.ts` for the * table's mapping). * * `info` is the fifth channel (2026-09-23): blue, on `--fp-banner-accent-info`, * the one hue here that carries no verdict. A state that is simply TRUE — * assigned, under way — and asks nothing of anybody. Grey would say it is * unremarkable; amber would say somebody is waiting. How an application binds * statuses to these five is `docs/ds/ui/2-rules.md` §10b. */ export type StatusTone = "success" | "processing" | "failed" | "neutral" | "info"; /** * Which of the status treatments to render. * text — the DEFAULT. Since 2026-10-09 it draws the PILL, as `soft` does. * soft — the PILL (`ui/pill.tsx`): rounded-full, 28px, a faint tint of the * tone's hue behind text in that hue. * dot — token-coloured dot BESIDE a neutral label. Asked for by name and * never arrived at by default: for a dense grid where many rows show * a status and a column of coloured words would shout. */ export type StatusChipVariant = "dot" | "text" | "soft"; /* EVERY STATUS IS A PILL (Pavan, 2026-10-09). `text` used to be the label alone in the tone colour and `soft` a smaller tinted chip; both now draw the DS pill, so a status reads the same in a table cell, a sheet header and on a board card. The tone is one of the DS's channels; the pill speaks in kinds, and this is the one place the two are matched. */ const TONE_KIND: Record = { success: "success", processing: "caution", failed: "critical", neutral: "neutral", info: "info", }; /** Dot fill per tone — only `dot` needs this; the others ride `bg-current`. */ const TONE_DOT: Record = { success: "bg-status-success", processing: "bg-status-processing", failed: "bg-status-failed", neutral: "bg-muted-foreground", info: "bg-fp-banner-accent-info", }; export interface StatusChipProps extends Omit, "color"> { /** The colour channel. Caller-supplied — the DS ships no status→tone map. */ tone?: StatusTone; variant?: StatusChipVariant; /** A colour the user chose (Sales stages), over the tone's — pill only. */ color?: PillColor | null; } /** * Status chip — one vocabulary for the three status treatments the system uses. * * The dot is `aria-hidden`: it repeats the label, so announcing it would just * add noise. Colour is never the only carrier of meaning — the label always * spells the status out. * * ```tsx * Success // the pill * Failed // the pill too * Queued // dot + neutral word * ``` * * CONTRAST — measured before 2026-10-09, when `text` and `soft` both became * the pill; the pill's ratios are the `soft` rows below. Label-vs-fill, both themes. `dot` keeps a * `foreground` label and is safe everywhere (14.6 dark / 20.5 light). * * variant/tone FP-dark Light (was -> now) * text/success 7.18 ok 3.30 FAILED -> 5.02 ok * text/processing 7.62 ok 3.19 FAILED -> 5.02 ok * text/failed 5.91 ok 4.83 ok (unchanged) * text/neutral 6.44 ok 5.99 ok (unchanged) * soft/success 6.04 ok 2.96 FAILED -> 4.38 ok for large only * soft/processing 6.38 ok 2.86 FAILED -> 4.39 ok for large only * soft/failed 5.15 ok 4.13 FAILED -> 4.13 still short * soft/neutral 5.45 ok 5.24 ok (unchanged) * * FIXED for `text`: the light `--status-success` / `--status-processing` values * moved one step down the ramp they already sit on (green-600 -> green-700, * amber-600 -> amber-700). Green and amber are far lighter than red/pink/blue at * the same step, which is why only those two needed it. See the note beside the * tokens in `src/index.css`. * * STILL SHORT for `soft` on light. A 10% tint of the label's own hue lifts the * background much faster than it darkens the text, so the pill lands at ~4.4 * rather than 4.5 — fine for large text, short of AA for body. `soft/failed` is * unchanged at 4.13. It used to be described as tracking `--destructive`; the * 2026-08-27 Figma light sync moved that token to red/500 (#ef4444, 3.76 as text * on white) while `--status-failed` deliberately stayed at red-600, so the two * are now independent and the `destructive` Badge variant no longer shares this * chip's recipe in light. If `soft` needs to * carry body text on light surfaces, the tint has to stop being a straight alpha * of the label colour — it needs its own token pair (a fixed tint plus a * foreground measured against it), the way the pastel pairs are built. Until * then `dot` and `text` are both safe on light and `soft` is large-text only. */ export function StatusChip({ tone = "neutral", variant = "text", color, className, children, ...props }: StatusChipProps) { const isPill = variant !== "dot"; return ( {/* A STATUS IS ITS WORD. The dot now renders for the `dot` variant and nowhere else, because that variant is the one place it is the ONLY thing carrying the tone — its label is deliberately neutral. `soft` tints the whole shape and `text` colours the whole label, so in both a dot of the same colour said the tone a second time and ate 12px of a chip whose whole job is to be small. Nothing is added to a status that the status has not been asked for: see `docs/ds/ui/2-rules.md` §11. */} {variant === "dot" && ( )} {isPill ? {children} : children} ); }
